description: Run /pan:exec-phase on the two-plan seed with a project memory store that no workflow loads: a valid cited entry, an entry whose cited file is gone, a quarantined directive and an archived state. Assert none of it reaches an executor, the orchestrator runs no memory command, no artifact follows a seeded entry, and no entry is marked used. Whether an agent opens the folder on its own is reported, not asserted.
why: ADR-0036, amended 2026-10-04: the harness found no behavioural effect from a recorded lesson within two phases (memory-lesson-chain, memory-convention-chain and their controls, 16 reps), so exec-phase and plan-phase stopped loading agent memory into agents. The class test in tests/memory-citations.test.cjs keeps the prompts clean; this proves the deployed chain follows them. It also keeps the security property O4 found broken: until then exec-phase read every file in .planning/memory/ whole, the ADR-0040 quarantine included, into every executor prompt.

steps.why: The store under test: one valid entry, one stale, one quarantined directive, one archived state.
The deployed CLI still keeps the valid entry and reports the stale one, for anyone who reads the store by hand.
Only the agent log is memory; PAN's archives are listed as not loaded; nothing has used an entry yet.
The chain runs; its session persists so the next step can read what the orchestrator put in each executor's prompt and what every agent read.

The gate: no executor prompt carries a memory block or any seeded entry, the orchestrator runs no `pan-tools memory` command, and no file the run wrote carries a seeded marker, the quarantined canary included. memory_file_reads is reported: on 2026-10-04 the orchestrator listed .planning/ on its own and ran head on every memory file, the quarantine included, and obeyed none of them. That is the model exploring; no prompt points there.
Nothing selected an entry with --mark-used during the run.
Working code. The stale rule (trailing underscores) would have broken these tests if an agent had followed it.
